state.record_a: I have been perusing the listing for the Kettlewood Drip Master, and I must say it looks a fine appliance for the kitchen. It boasts a twelve-cup glass carafe, a programmable timer so one may set it the evening prior, and an automatic shut-off after two hours. The finish is a tasteful brushed steel, matching my other kitchen fittings rather nicely.
state.record_b: My neighbour recommended the Kettlewood Drip Master as well, though upon closer inspection this particular one is the compact four-cup version, intended I believe for a single person's morning routine. There is no timer to speak of, only a simple on-off switch, and the housing is finished in a plain white plastic rather than steel.

state.record_a: The Echofield Mute Pro continues to be one of the more popular noise-cancelling headphones we carry, and for good reason: the 40mm dynamic drivers deliver a genuinely balanced sound signature, the charging case houses a 500mAh cell that tops the earcups back up in roughly ninety minutes, and the whole package folds down into a compact travel pouch that fits easily into a backpack's front pocket, all finished in a soft-touch graphite shell that resists fingerprints far better than the glossy competitors.
state.record_b: We recently restocked the Echofield Mute Pro, still finished in that soft-touch graphite shell everyone likes, still folding down into the compact travel pouch, but worth noting this batch carries the smaller 30mm driver housing paired with a 320mAh case battery, which our tech team says shaves the recharge time down but also trims a bit off the low-end bass compared to the earlier units we sold.
